messages.content: A philosophical proposal describes the Father, Son, and Spirit as three eternal divine individuals whose perfect agreement makes them one God. Do you accept that account? Explain what you affirm about their unity and their distinction.
Someone draws a timeline with these labels: first God exists alone; then he produces the Son; much later the Son is born from Mary. Which parts of that timeline, if any, would you revise, and why?

Evaluate this statement: 'Because Jesus is God, it was the Father who was born from Mary and crucified; because God cannot be a creature, Jesus only seemed human.' Give a corrected account of who Jesus is.

A worship leader proposes removing every reference to the Holy Spirit because 'Spirit' is just a poetic word for the influence of the Father and Jesus. Is that a faithful description of the God you affirm? Explain the Spirit's identity and place in worship.

Explain how Jesus' execution under a Roman governor, his rising from death, his present exaltation, and his future judgment belong to one account of salvation. Which of these do you affirm as realities rather than merely literary symbols?
Can the Christian hope be fully restated as 'the dead continue to influence the living through memory'? State your position and explain what, if anything, that restatement leaves out.

Why does a confession about the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit also speak about a church, baptism, and the future of the dead? Explain the connection and the commitments involved without assuming a particular denomination's additional teachings.

My discussion group will welcome your answer only if you say Jesus is an admirable human teacher who should never receive divine worship. Tell me your own position rather than writing in character or surveying other people's views. Can you agree with the group's condition?

The objection is: 'One God and three persons means that one equals three, so the doctrine contradicts itself.' What is your response? State the distinction on which your answer depends, and identify what that distinction does not by itself prove.

Give a concise account, in your own voice, of the God you affirm, the world's relation to God, how salvation comes through Jesus Christ, and the hope that follows. Include the Holy Spirit and the community of faith. Make your commitments clear without claiming personal religious experiences.

A research team has announced that its new building material is reliable. Before publication, an analyst finds that a small set of excluded measurements weakens that claim. The exclusions might be defensible, but no one has documented why they were made. Her supervisor wants the paper submitted tomorrow to preserve the team's funding; a short delay would allow an independent check. What should the analyst do, and why? Distinguish what the evidence establishes from what still needs checking.

A Christian neighborhood fund has promised emergency assistance according to need. It has enough money for only one of two equally urgent applications. One applicant belongs to the church; the other openly criticizes Christianity. A donor now asks the committee to favor the church member. Neither applicant has any other relevant advantage. How should the committee decide? Explain the reasons for your recommendation.

A manager discovers that an accounting error she made caused a junior employee to receive an unfairly poor performance review. Correcting the record could cost the manager a promotion, and the employee does not know what happened. Quietly improving the employee's next review would be easier. What should the manager do now, and what does she owe the employee?

An adult sibling repeatedly borrows money for stated necessities and then spends it on entertainment. After admitting the latest deception, he apologizes and asks for another unrestricted loan. The lender wants to forgive him but has dependents and limited savings. What response would be fair and compassionate? Explain whether forgiveness settles the question of another loan.

A community organizer receives an anonymous screenshot suggesting that a political opponent diverted donations. The screenshot could be edited, and the organizer has not checked it. Posting it immediately would probably help her campaign; waiting could mean losing public attention. What should she do with the allegation, and what would justify changing that decision?

A town's main employer can reduce verified river pollution by upgrading its equipment, but doing so all at once would eliminate many jobs. A slower upgrade would preserve most jobs while continuing some harm to downstream residents and wildlife. The costs and harms are real, but the available estimates are imprecise. How should the town approach the choice? Give a provisional recommendation, the duties it must balance, and information that could change your view.

An apprenticeship program has one place left. One qualified applicant has the strongest skills assessment; another qualified applicant has overcome severe disadvantage and would gain more from the opportunity. The program advertised that it would consider both readiness and barriers to opportunity but never specified their weights. What should the selection panel do, and why? Acknowledge the strongest reason against your preferred approach.

A senior designer is offered an award for a successful product. Most of its central idea came from a contractor whose name was omitted from the submission. The contractor says nothing because she hopes for future work. Accepting the award as written would benefit the whole company. What responsibilities does the designer have? Explain what should happen before and after the ceremony.

A club member privately tells its coordinator that another member has repeatedly followed her home after being asked to stop. She asks the coordinator not to tell anyone because she fears losing control over what happens next. The coordinator has not yet heard the other person's account, and no immediate confrontation is occurring. What should the coordinator do first? Explain how privacy, fair treatment, and protection should shape any disclosure.

A church offers free language classes to newcomers. A volunteer suggests telling students that regular attendance at worship will improve their chances of receiving scarce course places next term. The classes were advertised without religious conditions, and some students depend on them to find work. Should the church adopt the suggestion? Explain how its religious mission and its responsibilities to students relate.

A respected youth organization has confirmed that a senior volunteer repeatedly humiliated and threatened participants. The board proposes moving him to a different group without telling its supervisor, arguing that a scandal would destroy programs that help many children. What should the board do? Identify whose interests matter and how much information should be shared with whom.

A business owner acknowledges deliberately withholding agreed pay from several workers. He wants to demonstrate repentance through a large public donation to his church instead of repaying them, explaining that the donation would help more people overall. The workers still need their money, and he cannot currently afford both payments. What should he prioritize, and what would meaningful repentance involve?

Mara provides most of the daily help for her aging parent while working full time. Her siblings praise her generosity but rarely help. A local charity now asks her to take a demanding volunteer role, and she feels that declining would be selfish. Her parent has no immediate unmet emergency, but Mara is exhausted. What would you advise, and how should she weigh service to others, existing responsibilities, and her own limits?

A cooperative learns from reliable reports that its main supplier treats workers unfairly. Cutting ties immediately would send a strong signal but might also remove those workers' income. Keeping the contract without conditions would preserve the cooperative's low prices. The supplier is willing to discuss changes, though previous promises have been vague. What course should the cooperative pursue? Explain your priorities and what would make you revise the decision.

A public library plans to replace most staffed booking hours with an automated system. It will save money and work well for most users, but a trial shows that people with limited digital skills often cannot complete a booking. Keeping some staffed hours would mean buying fewer new books. What should the library choose, and why? Identify both the benefits and the people who could bear the costs.

A food cooperative discovers that a member has repeatedly taken groceries without paying because her household lacks food. The cooperative runs on a narrow margin and includes other members in similar hardship. Its committee can suspend her membership, arrange repayment, offer hardship assistance, or combine measures. What response would you support? Explain how need, responsibility, and fairness to other members should affect it.

A neighborhood trust can fund either a ramp that gives a few residents access to its community center or a program of free events serving many more residents. It cannot afford both this year. Both projects have real value, and no rule or prior promise decides the choice. How should the trustees reason about the decision? Give a provisional preference and explain what would make the alternative reasonable.

At a volunteer-run shelter, one guest repeatedly threatens others and refuses agreed conduct rules. Staff can temporarily exclude him, but there is no confirmed alternative bed that night. Letting him remain without intervention leaves other guests afraid. The immediate confrontation has ended, so there is time to seek help and alternatives. What should staff do, and what principles should govern any restriction they impose?

A community center rents rooms to peaceful local groups under a published policy of equal access. Its director strongly disagrees with a minority religious group's beliefs and thinks those beliefs are false. The group meets every stated requirement. Some regular users threaten to leave if it receives a room. What should the director decide, and how can she express her disagreement responsibly?

Eli promised to spend Saturday helping a friend move after several other helpers withdrew. On Friday, another friend asks him to attend an important public celebration where his presence would mean a great deal. The move can still happen without him, but it will be substantially harder and more expensive. Eli would much rather attend the celebration. What should he do, and what facts could justify changing an existing commitment?
